content: Destrin, also referred to as DSTN or actin depolymerizing factor (ADF), is a protein encoded by the DSTN gene in humans. This protein is a critical component of microfilaments within the cytoskeleton. The product of the DSTN gene belongs to the actin-binding protein family known as the ADF/cofilin family. Proteins in this family play a pivotal role in enhancing the turnover rate of actin filaments in vivo. The protein encoded by the DSTN gene functions as an actin depolymerizing factor. It is capable of severing actin filaments (F-actin) and binding to actin monomers (G-actin). Additionally, two transcript variants encoding distinct isoforms of destrin have been identified, indicating the existence of multiple functional forms of this protein. Structure The tertiary structure of destrin has been elucidated using advanced techniques such as triple-resonance multidimensional nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). The secondary and tertiary structures of destrin share similarities with the gelsolin family, another group of actin-regulating proteins. Destrin is a globular protein with a well-defined structural organization consisting of three ordered layers. At its core, destrin contains a central β-sheet composed of one parallel strand and three antiparallel strands. This β-sheet is flanked by a long α-helix and a shorter α-helix on one side, while two shorter helices are located on the opposite side. The four helices are arranged parallel to the β-strands, contributing to the protein's overall stability and functionality. Function Destrin plays a crucial role in regulating actin dynamics within the cytoskeleton of various eukaryotic cells. It binds to actin and is thought to interact with it in a manner similar to gelsolin segment-1. The binding of destrin and cofilin to actin is tightly regulated and is negatively influenced by phosphorylation, which modulates their activity. Furthermore, destrin has the ability to sever actin filaments, a function that is essential for the remodeling and turnover of the actin cytoskeleton.
